tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up

Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.

At most 100 characters.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

1	/**
2	 * The whole-DRKG neighbour data in `public/drkg/graph/` (contract: index.json,
3	 * ids.txt, names-extra.json, shard-NNN.bin). Every loader resolves to `null`
4	 * when its file is missing, so a fresh clone still gets the canvas and the
5	 * names.json search from `public/drkg/`.
6	 */
7	
8	export const GRAPH_DIR = '/drkg/graph/'
9	const MAGIC = 0x314b4744
10	
11	export type GraphIndex = {
12	  version: 1
13	  entities: number
14	  triples: number
15	  shardSize: number
16	  shards: number
17	  edgeCap: number
18	  knnK: number
19	  knnScope: string
20	  relations: { name: string; source: string; label: string; head: string; tail: string; count: number }[]
21	  types: { name: string; count: number }[]
22	  externalUrl: Record<string, string>
23	}
24	
25	type Shard = {
26	  firstRow: number
27	  knnK: number
28	  edgeOffsets: Uint32Array
29	  edges: Uint32Array
30	  relOffsets: Uint32Array
31	  relCounts: Uint32Array
32	  knnRows: Uint32Array
33	  knnDist: Float32Array
34	}
35	
36	/** One entity's slice of its shard; views, not copies. */
37	export type EntityGraph = { edges: Uint32Array; relCounts: Uint32Array; knnRows: Uint32Array; knnDist: Float32Array }
38	
39	export const edgeNbr = (e: number) => e & 0x1ffff
40	export const edgeRel = (e: number) => (e >>> 17) & 0x7f
41	export const edgeOut = (e: number) => ((e >>> 24) & 1) === 1
42	export const relIdx = (e: number) => e >>> 24
43	export const relCount = (e: number) => e & 0xffffff
44	
45	// Vite's dev server answers a missing file with index.html (200), so every
46	// loader validates its shape and maps anything wrong to null.
47	async function fetchOk(url: string) {
48	  const res = await fetch(url)
49	  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`${url}: ${res.status}`)
50	  return res
51	}
52	
53	function once<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>) {
54	  let p: Promise<T> | null = null
55	  return () => {
56	    p ??= fn().catch((e) => {
57	      p = null // a later call retries
58	      throw e
59	    })
60	    return p
61	  }
62	}
63	
64	export const loadIndex = once(async (): Promise<GraphIndex | null> => {
65	  try {
66	    const idx = (await (await fetchOk(GRAPH_DIR + 'index.json')).json()) as GraphIndex
67	    return idx?.version === 1 && idx.shardSize > 0 ? idx : null
68	  } catch {
69	    return null
70	  }
71	})
72	
73	export const loadIds = once(async (): Promise<string[] | null> => {
74	  try {
75	    const ids = (await (await fetchOk(GRAPH_DIR + 'ids.txt')).text()).split('\n')
76	    if (ids.at(-1) === '') ids.pop()
77	    return ids.length > 1000 && ids[0].includes('::') ? ids : null
78	  } catch {
79	    return null
80	  }
81	})
82	
83	export const loadNamesExtra = once(async (): Promise<Record<string, string>> => {
84	  try {
85	    return (await (await fetchOk(GRAPH_DIR + 'names-extra.json')).json()) as Record<string, string>
86	  } catch {
87	    return {}
88	  }
89	})

91	const shards = new Map<number, Promise<Shard>>()
92	
93	function loadShard(s: number) {
94	  let p = shards.get(s)
95	  if (p) return p
96	  p = fetchOk(`${GRAPH_DIR}shard-${String(s).padStart(3, '0')}.bin`)
97	    .then((r) => r.arrayBuffer())
98	    .then(decodeShard)
99	  shards.set(s, p)
100	  p.catch(() => shards.delete(s))
101	  return p
102	}
103	
104	export function decodeShard(buf: ArrayBuffer): Shard {
105	  const h = new Uint32Array(buf, 0, 8)
106	  if (h[0] !== MAGIC) throw new Error('not a DRKG graph shard')
107	  const [, firstRow, rowCount, nEdges, nRel, knnK] = h
108	  let o = 32
109	  const u32 = (n: number) => {
110	    const a = new Uint32Array(buf, o, n)
111	    o += n * 4
112	    return a
113	  }
114	  const edgeOffsets = u32(rowCount + 1)
115	  const edges = u32(nEdges)
116	  const relOffsets = u32(rowCount + 1)
117	  const relCounts = u32(nRel)
118	  const knnRows = u32(rowCount * knnK)
119	  const knnDist = new Float32Array(buf, o, rowCount * knnK)
120	  return { firstRow, knnK, edgeOffsets, edges, relOffsets, relCounts, knnRows, knnDist }
121	}
122	
123	export async function loadEntity(row: number, index: GraphIndex): Promise<EntityGraph> {
124	  const sh = await loadShard(Math.floor(row / index.shardSize))
125	  const i = row - sh.firstRow
126	  const k = sh.knnK
127	  return {
128	    edges: sh.edges.subarray(sh.edgeOffsets[i], sh.edgeOffsets[i + 1]),
129	    relCounts: sh.relCounts.subarray(sh.relOffsets[i], sh.relOffsets[i + 1]),
130	    knnRows: sh.knnRows.subarray(i * k, (i + 1) * k),
131	    knnDist: sh.knnDist.subarray(i * k, (i + 1) * k),
132	  }
133	}

135	/** Longest matching id prefix wins; `{id}` is what follows it. */
136	export function externalUrl(id: string, map: Record<string, string>) {
137	  let best = ''
138	  for (const p in map) if (id.startsWith(p) && p.length > best.length) best = p
139	  return best ? map[best].replace('{id}', encodeURIComponent(id.slice(best.length))) : null
140	}
141	
142	/* ----------------------------------------------------------------- search -- */
143	
144	export type SearchIndex = { label: string[]; lower: string[]; idLower: string[]; bare: string[] }
145	
146	/** `label[row]`: the best human name we have, falling back to the id's local part. */
147	export function buildSearch(n: number, names: Record<string, string>, extra: Record<string, string>, ids: string[] | null): SearchIndex {
148	  const label = new Array<string>(n)
149	  const lower = new Array<string>(n)
150	  const idLower = new Array<string>(n)
151	  const bare = new Array<string>(n)
152	  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
153	    const id = ids?.[i] ?? ''
154	    const l = names[i] ?? extra[i] ?? (id ? id.slice(id.indexOf('::') + 2) : '')
155	    label[i] = l
156	    lower[i] = l.toLowerCase()
157	    idLower[i] = id.toLowerCase()
158	    bare[i] = idLower[i].slice(idLower[i].indexOf('::') + 2)
159	  }
160	  return { label, lower, idLower, bare }
161	}
162	
163	const isWordChar = (c: number) => (c >= 48 && c <= 57) || (c >= 97 && c <= 122)
164	
165	/** 4 exact · 3 prefix · 2 word-prefix · 1 substring · 0 none. */
166	function score(s: string, q: string) {
167	  if (!s) return 0
168	  const at = s.indexOf(q)
169	  if (at < 0) return 0
170	  if (at === 0) return s.length === q.length ? 4 : 3
171	  for (let k = at; k >= 0; k = s.indexOf(q, k + 1)) if (!isWordChar(s.charCodeAt(k - 1))) return 2
172	  return 1
173	}
174	
175	/** Linear scan: ~97k `indexOf`, a few ms; ties by degree desc. */
176	export function search(q: string, idx: SearchIndex, degree: Uint32Array | null, types: Uint8Array, only: Set<number>, limit = 30) {
177	  const query = q.trim().toLowerCase()
178	  if (!query) return []
179	  const hits: number[] = []
180	  const scores = new Float64Array(idx.label.length)
181	  for (let i = 0; i < idx.label.length; i++) {
182	    if (only.size && !only.has(types[i])) continue
183	    const s = Math.max(score(idx.lower[i], query), score(idx.idLower[i], query), score(idx.bare[i], query))
184	    if (s) {
185	      hits.push(i)
186	      scores[i] = s * 1e7 + (degree ? Math.min(degree[i], 9_999_999) : 0)
187	    }
188	  }
189	  hits.sort((a, b) => scores[b] - scores[a])
190	  return hits.slice(0, limit)
191	}

23	/** OKLCH → sRGB hex (three can't parse oklch()). */
24	function oklch(l: number, c: number, hDeg: number) {
25	  const h = (hDeg * Math.PI) / 180
26	  const a = c * Math.cos(h)
27	  const b = c * Math.sin(h)
28	  const l_ = (l + 0.3963377774 * a + 0.2158037573 * b) ** 3
29	  const m_ = (l - 0.1055613458 * a - 0.0638541728 * b) ** 3
30	  const s_ = (l - 0.0894841775 * a - 1.291485548 * b) ** 3
31	  const lin = [
32	    4.0767416621 * l_ - 3.3077115913 * m_ + 0.2309699292 * s_,
33	    -1.2684380046 * l_ + 2.6097574011 * m_ - 0.3413193965 * s_,
34	    -0.0041960863 * l_ - 0.7034186147 * m_ + 1.707614701 * s_,
35	  ]
36	  const gamma = (x: number) => Math.round(255 * Math.min(1, Math.max(0, x <= 0.0031308 ? 12.92 * x : 1.055 * x ** (1 / 2.4) - 0.055)))
37	  return '#' + lin.map((x) => gamma(x).toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('')
38	}
39	/** Golden-angle hues; types a touch more saturated than stage 3's clusters so 13 stay apart. */
40	export const typeHex = (i: number) => oklch(0.66, 0.105, (i * 137.508 + 200) % 360)
41	export const clusterHex = (id: number, color?: string) => (color?.startsWith('#') ? color : oklch(0.7, 0.085, (id * 137.508 + 200) % 360))

50	const POINT_VERT = /* glsl */ `
51	  attribute vec3 color;
52	  attribute float aSize;
53	  attribute float aShape;
54	  attribute float aType;
55	  attribute float aHi;
56	  uniform float uPx;
57	  uniform float uDim;
58	  uniform float uPass[${MAX_TYPES}];
59	  uniform vec3 uPaper;
60	  varying vec3 vColor;
61	  varying float vAlpha;
62	  varying float vShape;
63	  void main() {
64	    vec4 mv = modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
65	    gl_Position = projectionMatrix * mv;
66	    float hi = step(0.5, aHi);
67	    float boost = aHi > 1.5 ? 2.2 : mix(1.0 - 0.45 * uDim, 1.5, hi);
68	    gl_PointSize = aSize * 0.75 * boost * uPx * (24.0 / -mv.z);
69	    float fog = smoothstep(18.0, 60.0, -mv.z) * 0.6 * (1.0 - hi);
70	    vColor = mix(color, uPaper, fog);
71	    float pass = uPass[int(aType + 0.5)];
72	    vAlpha = hi > 0.5 ? 1.0 : 0.7 * mix(0.045, 1.0, pass) * mix(1.0, 0.08, uDim);
73	    vShape = aShape;
74	  }
75	`
76	const POINT_FRAG = /* glsl */ `
77	  varying vec3 vColor;
78	  varying float vAlpha;
79	  varying float vShape;
80	  float edge(float d, float r, float aa) { return 1.0 - smoothstep(r - aa, r, d); }
81	  void main() {
82	    vec2 c = gl_PointCoord - 0.5;
83	    float d = length(c) * 2.0;
84	    float dd = (abs(c.x) + abs(c.y)) * 2.0;
85	    float aa = max(fwidth(d), 0.02) * 1.2;
86	    int s = int(vShape + 0.5);
87	    float a;
88	    if (s == 0) a = edge(d, 1.0, aa);                                   // compound: filled disc
89	    else if (s == 1) a = edge(d, 1.0, aa) * (1.0 - edge(d, 0.4, aa));  // gene: ring
90	    else if (s == 2) a = edge(dd, 0.95, aa);                            // disease: diamond
91	    else a = (1.0 - smoothstep(0.15, 0.55, d)) * 0.85;                  // other: soft dot
92	    a *= vAlpha;
93	    if (a <= 0.004) discard;
94	    gl_FragColor = vec4(vColor, a);
95	  }
96	`
97	// Selected entity: an ink ring at a constant on-screen size.
98	const HALO_VERT = /* glsl */ `
99	  uniform float uPx;
100	  void main() {
101	    gl_Position = projectionMatrix * modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
102	    gl_PointSize = 34.0 * uPx;
103	  }
104	`
105	const HALO_FRAG = /* glsl */ `
106	  uniform vec3 uInk;
107	  void main() {
108	    float d = length(gl_PointCoord - 0.5) * 2.0;
109	    float aa = fwidth(d) * 1.2;
110	    float ring = smoothstep(0.78 - aa, 0.78, d) * (1.0 - smoothstep(0.9, 0.9 + aa, d));
111	    if (ring <= 0.01) discard;
112	    gl_FragColor = vec4(uInk, ring * 0.9);
113	  }
114	`

1	/**
2	 * The whole-DRKG neighbour data in `public/drkg/graph/` (contract: index.json,
3	 * ids.txt, names-extra.json, shard-NNN.bin). Every loader resolves to `null`
4	 * when its file is missing, so a fresh clone still gets the canvas and the
5	 * names.json search from `public/drkg/`.
6	 */
7	
8	export const GRAPH_DIR = '/drkg/graph/'
9	const MAGIC = 0x314b4744
10	
11	export type GraphIndex = {
12	  version: 1
13	  entities: number
14	  triples: number
15	  shardSize: number
16	  shards: number
17	  edgeCap: number
18	  knnK: number
19	  knnScope: string
20	  relations: { name: string; source: string; label: string; head: string; tail: string; count: number }[]
21	  types: { name: string; count: number }[]
22	  externalUrl: Record<string, string>
23	}
24	
25	type Shard = {
26	  firstRow: number
27	  knnK: number
28	  edgeOffsets: Uint32Array
29	  edges: Uint32Array
30	  relOffsets: Uint32Array
31	  relCounts: Uint32Array
32	  knnRows: Uint32Array
33	  knnDist: Float32Array
34	}
35	
36	/** One entity's slice of its shard; views, not copies. */
37	export type EntityGraph = { edges: Uint32Array; relCounts: Uint32Array; knnRows: Uint32Array; knnDist: Float32Array }
38	
39	export const edgeNbr = (e: number) => e & 0x1ffff
40	export const edgeRel = (e: number) => (e >>> 17) & 0x7f
41	export const edgeOut = (e: number) => ((e >>> 24) & 1) === 1
42	export const relIdx = (e: number) => e >>> 24
43	export const relCount = (e: number) => e & 0xffffff
44	
45	// Vite's dev server answers a missing file with index.html (200), so every
46	// loader validates its shape and maps anything wrong to null.
47	async function fetchOk(url: string) {
48	  const res = await fetch(url)
49	  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`${url}: ${res.status}`)
50	  return res
51	}
52	
53	function once<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>) {
54	  let p: Promise<T> | null = null
55	  return () => {
56	    p ??= fn().catch((e) => {
57	      p = null // a later call retries
58	      throw e
59	    })
60	    return p
61	  }
62	}
63	
64	export const loadIndex = once(async (): Promise<GraphIndex | null> => {
65	  try {
66	    const idx = (await (await fetchOk(GRAPH_DIR + 'index.json')).json()) as GraphIndex
67	    return idx?.version === 1 && idx.shardSize > 0 ? idx : null
68	  } catch {
69	    return null
70	  }
71	})
72	
73	export const loadIds = once(async (): Promise<string[] | null> => {
74	  try {
75	    const ids = (await (await fetchOk(GRAPH_DIR + 'ids.txt')).text()).split('\n')
76	    if (ids.at(-1) === '') ids.pop()
77	    return ids.length > 1000 && ids[0].includes('::') ? ids : null
78	  } catch {
79	    return null
80	  }
81	})
82	
83	export const loadNamesExtra = once(async (): Promise<Record<string, string>> => {
84	  try {
85	    return (await (await fetchOk(GRAPH_DIR + 'names-extra.json')).json()) as Record<string, string>
86	  } catch {
87	    return {}
88	  }
89	})
90	
91	const shards = new Map<number, Promise<Shard>>()
92	
93	function loadShard(s: number) {
94	  let p = shards.get(s)
95	  if (p) return p
96	  p = fetchOk(`${GRAPH_DIR}shard-${String(s).padStart(3, '0')}.bin`)
97	    .then((r) => r.arrayBuffer())
98	    .then(decodeShard)
99	  shards.set(s, p)
100	  p.catch(() => shards.delete(s))
101	  return p
102	}
103	
104	export function decodeShard(buf: ArrayBuffer): Shard {
105	  const h = new Uint32Array(buf, 0, 8)
106	  if (h[0] !== MAGIC) throw new Error('not a DRKG graph shard')
107	  const [, firstRow, rowCount, nEdges, nRel, knnK] = h
108	  let o = 32
109	  const u32 = (n: number) => {
110	    const a = new Uint32Array(buf, o, n)
111	    o += n * 4
112	    return a
113	  }
114	  const edgeOffsets = u32(rowCount + 1)
115	  const edges = u32(nEdges)
116	  const relOffsets = u32(rowCount + 1)
117	  const relCounts = u32(nRel)
118	  const knnRows = u32(rowCount * knnK)
119	  const knnDist = new Float32Array(buf, o, rowCount * knnK)
120	  return { firstRow, knnK, edgeOffsets, edges, relOffsets, relCounts, knnRows, knnDist }
121	}
122	
123	export async function loadEntity(row: number, index: GraphIndex): Promise<EntityGraph> {
124	  const sh = await loadShard(Math.floor(row / index.shardSize))
125	  const i = row - sh.firstRow
126	  const k = sh.knnK
127	  return {
128	    edges: sh.edges.subarray(sh.edgeOffsets[i], sh.edgeOffsets[i + 1]),
129	    relCounts: sh.relCounts.subarray(sh.relOffsets[i], sh.relOffsets[i + 1]),
130	    knnRows: sh.knnRows.subarray(i * k, (i + 1) * k),
131	    knnDist: sh.knnDist.subarray(i * k, (i + 1) * k),
132	  }
133	}
134	
135	/** Longest matching id prefix wins; `{id}` is what follows it. */
136	export function externalUrl(id: string, map: Record<string, string>) {
137	  let best = ''
138	  for (const p in map) if (id.startsWith(p) && p.length > best.length) best = p
139	  return best ? map[best].replace('{id}', encodeURIComponent(id.slice(best.length))) : null
140	}
141	
142	/* ----------------------------------------------------------------- search -- */
143	
144	export type SearchIndex = { label: string[]; lower: string[]; idLower: string[]; bare: string[] }
145	
146	/** `label[row]`: the best human name we have, falling back to the id's local part. */
147	export function buildSearch(n: number, names: Record<string, string>, extra: Record<string, string>, ids: string[] | null): SearchIndex {
148	  const label = new Array<string>(n)
149	  const lower = new Array<string>(n)
150	  const idLower = new Array<string>(n)
151	  const bare = new Array<string>(n)
152	  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
153	    const id = ids?.[i] ?? ''
154	    const l = names[i] ?? extra[i] ?? (id ? id.slice(id.indexOf('::') + 2) : '')
155	    label[i] = l
156	    lower[i] = l.toLowerCase()
157	    idLower[i] = id.toLowerCase()
158	    bare[i] = idLower[i].slice(idLower[i].indexOf('::') + 2)
159	  }
160	  return { label, lower, idLower, bare }
161	}
162	
163	const isWordChar = (c: number) => (c >= 48 && c <= 57) || (c >= 97 && c <= 122)
164	
165	/** 4 exact · 3 prefix · 2 word-prefix · 1 substring · 0 none. */
166	function score(s: string, q: string) {
167	  if (!s) return 0
168	  const at = s.indexOf(q)
169	  if (at < 0) return 0
170	  if (at === 0) return s.length === q.length ? 4 : 3
171	  for (let k = at; k >= 0; k = s.indexOf(q, k + 1)) if (!isWordChar(s.charCodeAt(k - 1))) return 2
172	  return 1
173	}
174	
175	/** Linear scan: ~97k `indexOf`, a few ms; ties by degree desc. */
176	export function search(q: string, idx: SearchIndex, degree: Uint32Array | null, types: Uint8Array, only: Set<number>, limit = 30) {
177	  const query = q.trim().toLowerCase()
178	  if (!query) return []
179	  const hits: number[] = []
180	  const scores = new Float64Array(idx.label.length)
181	  for (let i = 0; i < idx.label.length; i++) {
182	    if (only.size && !only.has(types[i])) continue
183	    const s = Math.max(score(idx.lower[i], query), score(idx.idLower[i], query), score(idx.bare[i], query))
184	    if (s) {
185	      hits.push(i)
186	      scores[i] = s * 1e7 + (degree ? Math.min(degree[i], 9_999_999) : 0)
187	    }
188	  }
189	  hits.sort((a, b) => scores[b] - scores[a])
190	  return hits.slice(0, limit)
191	}
192	
193	/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- self-test -- */
194	
195	if (import.meta.env?.DEV && typeof window !== 'undefined' && !(window as { __graphDataTested?: boolean }).__graphDataTested) {
196	  ;(window as { __graphDataTested?: boolean }).__graphDataTested = true
197	  const e = 70000 | (5 << 17) | (1 << 24)
198	  console.assert(edgeNbr(e) === 70000 && edgeRel(e) === 5 && edgeOut(e), 'edge decode')
199	  console.assert(relIdx((9 << 24) | 1234) === 9 && relCount((9 << 24) | 1234) === 1234, 'relCount decode')
200	  console.assert(score('riluzole', 'riluzole') === 4 && score('riluzole tab', 'ril') === 3 && score('acid riluzole', 'ril') === 2 && score('xriluzole', 'ril') === 1, 'score tiers')
201	  console.assert(externalUrl('Gene::6647', { 'Gene::': 'g/{id}', 'Gene::66': 'x/{id}' }) === 'x/47', 'longest prefix')
202	}

9	/**
10	 * All 97,238 DRKG entities as one THREE.Points. Same visual grammar as the
11	 * stage-3 scene: position = clustered TransE layout, colour = type or cluster,
12	 * size = log degree, shape = type (Compound ● · Gene ○ · Disease ◆ · other ·).
13	 * Selection is a sparse `aHi` attribute plus a `uDim` uniform, never a rewrite
14	 * of all colours.
15	 */
16	
17	const MAX_TYPES = 16
18	const PAPER = new THREE.Color('#f7f4ee')
19	const INK = '#13293d'
20	
21	/* --------------------------------------------------------------- colours -- */
22	
23	/** OKLCH → sRGB hex (three can't parse oklch()). */
24	function oklch(l: number, c: number, hDeg: number) {
25	  const h = (hDeg * Math.PI) / 180
26	  const a = c * Math.cos(h)
27	  const b = c * Math.sin(h)
28	  const l_ = (l + 0.3963377774 * a + 0.2158037573 * b) ** 3
29	  const m_ = (l - 0.1055613458 * a - 0.0638541728 * b) ** 3
30	  const s_ = (l - 0.0894841775 * a - 1.291485548 * b) ** 3
31	  const lin = [
32	    4.0767416621 * l_ - 3.3077115913 * m_ + 0.2309699292 * s_,
33	    -1.2684380046 * l_ + 2.6097574011 * m_ - 0.3413193965 * s_,
34	    -0.0041960863 * l_ - 0.7034186147 * m_ + 1.707614701 * s_,
35	  ]
36	  const gamma = (x: number) => Math.round(255 * Math.min(1, Math.max(0, x <= 0.0031308 ? 12.92 * x : 1.055 * x ** (1 / 2.4) - 0.055)))
37	  return '#' + lin.map((x) => gamma(x).toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('')
38	}
39	/** Golden-angle hues; types a touch more saturated than stage 3's clusters so 13 stay apart. */
40	export const typeHex = (i: number) => oklch(0.66, 0.105, (i * 137.508 + 200) % 360)
41	export const clusterHex = (id: number, color?: string) => (color?.startsWith('#') ? color : oklch(0.7, 0.085, (id * 137.508 + 200) % 360))
42	
43	const shapeOf = (type: string) => (type === 'Compound' ? 0 : type === 'Gene' ? 1 : type === 'Disease' ? 2 : 3)
44	
45	/** Entity-type glyph: stage 3's, so both views draw types identically and never by colour alone. */
46	export { TypeGlyph }
47	
48	/* --------------------------------------------------------------- shaders -- */
49	
50	const POINT_VERT = /* glsl */ `
51	  attribute vec3 color;
52	  attribute float aSize;
53	  attribute float aShape;
54	  attribute float aType;
55	  attribute float aHi;
56	  uniform float uPx;
57	  uniform float uDim;
58	  uniform float uPass[${MAX_TYPES}];
59	  uniform vec3 uPaper;
60	  varying vec3 vColor;
61	  varying float vAlpha;
62	  varying float vShape;
63	  void main() {
64	    vec4 mv = modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
65	    gl_Position = projectionMatrix * mv;
66	    float hi = step(0.5, aHi);
67	    float boost = aHi > 1.5 ? 2.2 : mix(1.0 - 0.45 * uDim, 1.5, hi);
68	    gl_PointSize = aSize * 0.75 * boost * uPx * (24.0 / -mv.z);
69	    float fog = smoothstep(18.0, 60.0, -mv.z) * 0.6 * (1.0 - hi);
70	    vColor = mix(color, uPaper, fog);
71	    float pass = uPass[int(aType + 0.5)];
72	    vAlpha = hi > 0.5 ? 1.0 : 0.7 * mix(0.045, 1.0, pass) * mix(1.0, 0.08, uDim);
73	    vShape = aShape;
74	  }
75	`
76	const POINT_FRAG = /* glsl */ `
77	  varying vec3 vColor;
78	  varying float vAlpha;
79	  varying float vShape;
80	  float edge(float d, float r, float aa) { return 1.0 - smoothstep(r - aa, r, d); }
81	  void main() {
82	    vec2 c = gl_PointCoord - 0.5;
83	    float d = length(c) * 2.0;
84	    float dd = (abs(c.x) + abs(c.y)) * 2.0;
85	    float aa = max(fwidth(d), 0.02) * 1.2;
86	    int s = int(vShape + 0.5);
87	    float a;
88	    if (s == 0) a = edge(d, 1.0, aa);                                   // compound: filled disc
89	    else if (s == 1) a = edge(d, 1.0, aa) * (1.0 - edge(d, 0.4, aa));  // gene: ring
90	    else if (s == 2) a = edge(dd, 0.95, aa);                            // disease: diamond
91	    else a = (1.0 - smoothstep(0.15, 0.55, d)) * 0.85;                  // other: soft dot
92	    a *= vAlpha;
93	    if (a <= 0.004) discard;
94	    gl_FragColor = vec4(vColor, a);
95	  }
96	`
97	// Selected entity: an ink ring at a constant on-screen size.
98	const HALO_VERT = /* glsl */ `
99	  uniform float uPx;
100	  void main() {
101	    gl_Position = projectionMatrix * modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
102	    gl_PointSize = 34.0 * uPx;
103	  }
104	`
105	const HALO_FRAG = /* glsl */ `
106	  uniform vec3 uInk;
107	  void main() {
108	    float d = length(gl_PointCoord - 0.5) * 2.0;
109	    float aa = fwidth(d) * 1.2;
110	    float ring = smoothstep(0.78 - aa, 0.78, d) * (1.0 - smoothstep(0.9, 0.9 + aa, d));
111	    if (ring <= 0.01) discard;
112	    gl_FragColor = vec4(uInk, ring * 0.9);
113	  }
114	`

# Interface

This skill runs a cross-discipline review. It routes the interface to each `better-*` skill, collects their evidence and consolidates one ranked verdict.

Change-scoped review of uncommitted work, branches and pull requests belongs to `interface-review`.

## Evidence, not taste

Press hard on the escalation triggers and leave deliberate project choices alone. A trigger is a failure whatever the style guide says. A density, radius or voice you merely disagree with is not a finding.

The bar for reporting is evidence. The bar for `Approve` is that you inspected what you claim to have inspected.

## 1. Resolve the scope first

Infer the screen, flow, feature or repository scope from the request and current workspace. State the resolved scope in the output.

Cover all of it in every domain, including the empty, loading, error and narrow-width states where they exist.

When the scope is too large to inspect credibly, narrow it to one complete flow. Take the one the request centers on, or failing that the entry path every user must pass through. State the boundary and what it excluded. Never imply uninspected surfaces were reviewed.

## 2. Send a change to `interface-review`

A request naming a branch, pull request, commit range or uncommitted changes is a change review. Say so and ask the user to run `interface-review`, which is user-invoked and cannot be started from here. Never resolve a change scope yourself, because a guessed diff gives the report a scope nobody can check.

When `interface-review` hands a review back, apply everything below to it. The cap and the verdict cover `Introduced` and `Regression` findings only, so a change whose only findings are `Pre-existing` is an `Approve`.

## 3. Recon before judgment

Identify the framework, styling system, component library, design tokens, supported viewports and any preview or test command. Write every fix in the project's own idiom, never as a request to adopt a different stack.

Then read what the project has written about its own interface: `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CODING_STANDARDS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, a design-system doc, Storybook docs and interface ADRs. Name which you found, or that there are none.

A documented convention settles matters of taste but never excuses a trigger or a domain rule violation. What it changes is **where** you report. When a guideline or shared token is the cause, report it once against that source, with the components as its locations.

## 4. Use domain skills as the sources of truth

Load every owning skill below and complete each domain review before consolidation. Review in this order so foundational failures are not hidden by polish:

1. `better-accessibility`
2. `better-layout`
3. `better-writing`
4. `better-typography`
5. `better-colors`
6. `better-ui`

From each, take its principles, its references and its verification checks. Its severity ladder and its format are for standalone use; the ones in this file replace them.

If an owning skill is unavailable, mark that domain `Not reviewed`, name it and continue with the rest. Do not recreate its rules from memory, substitute a neighbour or claim holistic coverage.

When two skills appear to cover one issue, assign it to the owner of the underlying rule and note secondary effects in the **Why** cell.

## 5. Verify what can be verified

Run the safe, relevant checks the project offers. Inspect the rendered interface when runtime behavior or visual judgment matters, and report the exact command or interaction and its result. A check you cannot run is **Not verified**, never a finding.

## Require evidence

Every finding cites `path/to/file:line` and shows the current implementation. When runtime behavior determines the result, source alone cannot support a visual finding and a screenshot alone cannot support a code finding.

## Rank by user impact

Use one shared severity scale:

- `HIGH`: blocks a task, misleads the user, hides content or controls, causes data-loss risk or creates a repeated systemic failure.
- `MEDIUM`: meaningfully harms comprehension, efficiency, adaptability or consistency.
- `LOW`: isolated polish with limited task impact.

Within a severity, rank by how many places the finding reaches and how much one fix buys. A token or shared-component fix outranks the same symptom in one leaf.

**Escalation triggers.** Once the owning skill confirms one of these, it is `HIGH` on sight, never averaged down because the surface is minor:

- An interactive control with no accessible name.
- A keyboard-reachable control with no visible focus indicator.
- A control or path reachable by pointer but not by keyboard.
- Motion or auto-playing content that ignores `prefers-reduced-motion`.

- Body or control text whose rendered contrast pair fails its required ratio.
- State or meaning carried by color alone.
- A destructive action with no confirmation, undo or distinct treatment.
- Truncated content with no way to reach the full value.
- Content or a control reachable only past a scroll edge or behind a disclosure that has no visible cue.

# fixing-motion-performance

Fix animation performance issues.

## how to use

- `/fixing-motion-performance`
  Apply these constraints to any UI animation work in this conversation.

- `/fixing-motion-performance <file>`
  Review the file against all rules below and report:
  - violations (quote the exact line or snippet)
  - why it matters (one short sentence)
  - a concrete fix (code-level suggestion)

Do not migrate animation libraries unless explicitly requested. Apply rules within the existing stack.

## when to apply

Reference these guidelines when:
- adding or changing UI animations (CSS, WAAPI, Motion, rAF, GSAP)
- refactoring janky interactions or transitions
- implementing scroll-linked motion or reveal-on-scroll
- animating layout, filters, masks, gradients, or CSS variables
- reviewing components that use will-change, transforms, or measurement

## rendering steps glossary

- composite: transform, opacity
- paint: color, borders, gradients, masks, images, filters
- layout: size, position, flow, grid, flex

## rule categories by priority

| priority | category | impact |
|----------|----------|--------|
| 1 | never patterns | critical |
| 2 | choose the mechanism | critical |
| 3 | measurement | high |
| 4 | scroll | high |
| 5 | paint | medium-high |
| 6 | layers | medium |
| 7 | blur and filters | medium |
| 8 | view transitions | low |
| 9 | tool boundaries | critical |

## quick reference

### 1. never patterns (critical)

- do not interleave layout reads and writes in the same frame
- do not animate layout continuously on large or meaningful surfaces
- do not drive animation from scrollTop, scrollY, or scroll events
- no requestAnimationFrame loops without a stop condition
- do not mix multiple animation systems that each measure or mutate layout

### 2. choose the mechanism (critical)

- default to transform and opacity for motion
- use JS-driven animation only when interaction requires it
- paint or layout animation is acceptable only on small, isolated surfaces
- one-shot effects are acceptable more often than continuous motion
- prefer downgrading technique over removing motion entirely

### 3. measurement (high)

- measure once, then animate via transform or opacity
- batch all DOM reads before writes
- do not read layout repeatedly during an animation
- prefer FLIP-style transitions for layout-like effects
- prefer approaches that batch measurement and writes

### 4. scroll (high)

- prefer Scroll or View Timelines for scroll-linked motion when available
- use IntersectionObserver for visibility and pausing
- do not poll scroll position for animation
- pause or stop animations when off-screen
- scroll-linked motion must not trigger continuous layout or paint on large surfaces

### 5. paint (medium-high)

- paint-triggering animation is allowed only on small, isolated elements
- do not animate paint-heavy properties on large containers
- do not animate CSS variables for transform, opacity, or position
- do not animate inherited CSS variables
- scope animated CSS variables locally and avoid inheritance

### 6. layers (medium)

- compositor motion requires layer promotion, never assume it
- use will-change temporarily and surgically
- avoid many or large promoted layers
- validate layer behavior with tooling when performance matters

### 7. blur and filters (medium)

- keep blur animation small (<=8px)
- use blur only for short, one-time effects
- never animate blur continuously
- never animate blur on large surfaces
- prefer opacity and translate before blur

### 8. view transitions (low)

- use view transitions only for navigation-level changes
- avoid view transitions for interaction-heavy UI
- avoid view transitions when interruption or cancellation is required
- treat size changes as potentially layout-triggering

### 9. tool boundaries (critical)

- do not migrate or rewrite animation libraries unless explicitly requested
- apply these rules within the existing animation system
- never partially migrate APIs or mix styles within the same component

## common fixes

```css
/* layout thrashing: animate transform instead of width */
/* before */ .panel { transition: width 0.3s; }
/* after */  .panel { transition: transform 0.3s; }

/* scroll-linked: use scroll-timeline instead of JS */
/* before */ window.addEventListener('scroll', () => el.style.opacity = scrollY / 500)
/* after */  .reveal { animation: fade-in linear; animation-timeline: view(); }
```

```js
// measurement: batch reads before writes (FLIP)
// before — layout thrash
el.style.left = el.getBoundingClientRect().left + 10 + 'px';
// after — measure once, animate via transform
const first = el.getBoundingClientRect();
el.classList.add('moved');
const last = el.getBoundingClientRect();
el.style.transform = `translateX(${first.left - last.left}px)`;
requestAnimationFrame(() => { el.style.transition = 'transform 0.3s'; el.style.transform = ''; });
```

## review guidance

- enforce critical rules first (never patterns, tool boundaries)
- choose the least expensive rendering work that matches the intent
- for any non-default choice, state the constraint that justifies it (surface size, duration, or interaction requirement)
- when reviewing, prefer actionable notes and concrete alternatives over theory

input.summary:
Read-only design and code review of frontend/src/components/graph/* (graph-canvas, graph-data, graph-explorer, graph-inspector, graph-search) and the committed Home.tsx hook (e507c8a). I loaded the better-interface and fixing-motion-performance skills. I did not load better-accessibility, -layout, -writing, -typography, -colors or -ui separately, so those domains are covered only through the AGENTS.md rules. I used no browser, so every rendering claim is Not verified at runtime.

What I verified:
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` passes with no output. The UI agent's warning about an unused `const bare` is stale: `bare` is used at graph-data.ts:158/160/183.
- I decoded shards 25, 10 and 0 in node using the UI's own layout. Byte totals match the file sizes exactly. index.json types are in the same order as scene.json types. ids.txt has 97,238 lines with no trailing newline.
- All five STARTS ids resolve and are labelled.
- The keyboard listeners are removed on unmount, so they don't leak to other views.
- GPU objects are disposed: geometries are swapped and the old ones disposed.
- The `aHi` update path is fine. A full 389 KB upload per selection is acceptable for scattered rows.
- The raycast threshold of 0.09 is about 1.8 px at the home distance (~40 units) and about 10 px at the 7-unit selection framing. That is close to the rendered point radius, so it is acceptable.
- No dark mode exists, so the hard-coded PAPER and INK colours are fine.

Ranked findings follow. The two to fix first are the shader colour space and the StrictMode OrbitControls lifecycle. The second one can be confirmed in the browser in about 10 seconds.

findings.area: React/three correctness: OrbitControls lifecycle under StrictMode (dev server)
findings.issue: OrbitControls is constructed inside useMemo, and its constructor attaches DOM listeners. It is then disposed in an effect cleanup. main.tsx wraps the app in <StrictMode>, and R3F v9 passes StrictMode into the Canvas: node_modules/@react-three/fiber/dist/events-*.cjs.dev.js:99 says it 'Bridges Context, StrictMode'. In dev, React therefore runs useMemo twice, and the throwaway instance #1 stays connected with its own target at (0,0,0). React also runs mount→cleanup→mount, so the kept instance #2 gets dispose()d (that is disconnect(), OrbitControls.js:511-540) and is never reconnected. Result: drag and wheel are handled by #1, which orbits (0,0,0) with no per-frame damping update. useFrame drives #2, which keeps target = home or selection. After selecting an entity, orbiting pivots around the wrong point and the camera snaps between the two targets. Production builds are unaffected, but the expo demo probably runs on `npm run dev`. drkg-scene.tsx:387-398 uses the same pattern (other session's file, not to edit).
findings.evidence: graph-canvas.tsx:145-165: `const controls = useMemo(() => { const c = new OrbitControls(camera, gl.domElement) ... }, [camera, gl])` then `useEffect(() => () => controls.dispose(), [controls])`. main.tsx:14 is `<StrictMode>`. PLAUSIBLE, not verified in the browser. Confirm on :5178 by selecting SOD1 and dragging: it should orbit SOD1.
findings.fix: Create the controls in an effect and keep them in a ref, e.g. `const controls = useRef<OrbitControls>(null); useEffect(() => { const c = new OrbitControls(camera, gl.domElement); /* settings + listeners */ controls.current = c; return () => c.dispose() }, [camera, gl])`, and guard `controls.current` in useFrame and the home effect. The alternative is to keep useMemo but call `controls.connect(gl.domElement)` in the effect body. That fixes the disposed instance but not the leaked duplicate, so the ref version is better.

findings.area: Colour correctness: point colours don't match the legend
findings.issue: Type and cluster colours go through `new THREE.Color(hex)`. ColorManagement is on by default in three 0.187, so this converts sRGB to linear. POINT_FRAG and HALO_FRAG then write gl_FragColor without `#include <colorspace_fragment>`, and ShaderMaterial does not convert to the sRGB output itself. The dots therefore display the linear values as sRGB, which makes them much darker and muddier than the TypeGlyph swatches in the legend, search rows and inspector (those use the CSS hex). The edge lines use LineBasicMaterial, which does convert, so lines and dots of the same type also disagree. The PAPER fog colour shifts the same way.
findings.evidence: I computed it with three's own Color: type 0 Gene legend #24a5ab → shader writes #046068; 1 Compound #bc78a9 → #803065; 3 Side Effect #6196d1 → #1e4ea3; 4 Disease #ca796b → #973125. graph-canvas.tsx:94 `gl_FragColor = vec4(vColor, a);` and :112 have no colorspace include. Canvas at :514 has no `linear`/`flat`.
findings.fix: Add one line after each gl_FragColor assignment in POINT_FRAG and HALO_FRAG: `#include <colorspace_fragment>`. Don't touch the global ColorManagement or add `<Canvas linear>`, because both are global and would change the stage-3 scene.

findings.area: Colour as sole carrier (AGENTS working style; better-interface trigger)
findings.issue: Only Compound, Gene and Disease get their own shapes. The other 10 types all share the same soft dot, both in the canvas and in the legend's TypeGlyph, so colour alone separates them. Golden-angle hues at a fixed L/C make index i and i+8 land only 20° apart, and i and i+5 land 32.5° apart. That produces near-identical pairs that also share a shape: Biological Process (2, #909a4a) vs Anatomy (10, #76a15e), Side Effect (3, #6196d1) vs Pharmacologic Class (11, #7c8ed3), Side Effect vs Cellular Component (8, #33a1bf), Molecular Function (6, #a181c6) vs Pharmacologic Class (11).
findings.evidence: graph-canvas.tsx:40 `typeHex = (i) => oklch(0.66, 0.105, (i * 137.508 + 200) % 360)`. :43 `shapeOf` returns 3 for every non-Compound/Gene/Disease type. Type order is from scene.json.
findings.fix: Cheapest fix: pick hues per type by hand from a 13-entry constant instead of the golden angle, keeping same-shape types at least 60° apart. Then rely on the existing type filter and hover tooltip as the non-colour path, and say so in the legend, e.g. 'click a type to isolate it'. Optionally give the four largest 'other' types (Biological Process, Side Effect, Atc, Molecular Function) a square or ring variant, both in the shader and in TypeGlyph.

findings.area: Motion performance and legibility: backdrop blur and translucency over an animated background
findings.issue: The canvas card and the aside use `bg-card` (which is `oklch(... / 0.76)`) plus `backdrop-blur-md`. They sit over GradientASCII, a second WebGL context that animates every frame (background.tsx; GradientASCII rAF at :813). That means two large backdrop-filter surfaces are re-blurred every frame. findings.area: Colour correctness: point colours don't match the legend
findings.issue: Type and cluster colours go through `new THREE.Color(hex)`. ColorManagement is on by default in three 0.187, so this converts sRGB to linear. POINT_FRAG and HALO_FRAG then write gl_FragColor without `#include <colorspace_fragment>`, and ShaderMaterial does not convert to the sRGB output itself. The dots therefore display the linear values as sRGB, which makes them much darker and muddier than the TypeGlyph swatches in the legend, search rows and inspector (those use the CSS hex). The edge lines use LineBasicMaterial, which does convert, so lines and dots of the same type also disagree. The PAPER fog colour shifts the same way.
findings.evidence: I computed it with three's own Color: type 0 Gene legend #24a5ab → shader writes #046068; 1 Compound #bc78a9 → #803065; 3 Side Effect #6196d1 → #1e4ea3; 4 Disease #ca796b → #973125. graph-canvas.tsx:94 `gl_FragColor = vec4(vColor, a);` and :112 have no colorspace include. Canvas at :514 has no `linear`/`flat`.
findings.fix: Add one line after each gl_FragColor assignment in POINT_FRAG and HALO_FRAG: `#include <colorspace_fragment>`. Don't touch the global ColorManagement or add `<Canvas linear>`, because both are global and would change the stage-3 scene.

findings.area: Colour as sole carrier (AGENTS working style; better-interface trigger)
findings.issue: Only Compound, Gene and Disease get their own shapes. The other 10 types all share the same soft dot, both in the canvas and in the legend's TypeGlyph, so colour alone separates them. Golden-angle hues at a fixed L/C make index i and i+8 land only 20° apart, and i and i+5 land 32.5° apart. That produces near-identical pairs that also share a shape: Biological Process (2, #909a4a) vs Anatomy (10, #76a15e), Side Effect (3, #6196d1) vs Pharmacologic Class (11, #7c8ed3), Side Effect vs Cellular Component (8, #33a1bf), Molecular Function (6, #a181c6) vs Pharmacologic Class (11).
findings.evidence: graph-canvas.tsx:40 `typeHex = (i) => oklch(0.66, 0.105, (i * 137.508 + 200) % 360)`. :43 `shapeOf` returns 3 for every non-Compound/Gene/Disease type. Type order is from scene.json.
findings.fix: Cheapest fix: pick hues per type by hand from a 13-entry constant instead of the golden angle, keeping same-shape types at least 60° apart. Then rely on the existing type filter and hover tooltip as the non-colour path, and say so in the legend, e.g. 'click a type to isolate it'. Optionally give the four largest 'other' types (Biological Process, Side Effect, Atc, Molecular Function) a square or ring variant, both in the shader and in TypeGlyph.

findings.area: Motion performance and legibility: backdrop blur and translucency over an animated background
findings.issue: The canvas card and the aside use `bg-card` (which is `oklch(... / 0.76)`) plus `backdrop-blur-md`. They sit over GradientASCII, a second WebGL context that animates every frame (background.tsx; GradientASCII rAF at :813). That means two large backdrop-filter surfaces are re-blurred every frame. The canvas has `alpha: true`, so the moving ASCII field also shows through behind the dust-sized points, which hurts contrast. On top of that, all ~24 island labels (`backdrop-blur-[2px]`) and the entity pills (`backdrop-blur-sm`) move by transform every frame, so roughly 35 continuously moving backdrop-filter layers sit over WebGL. This breaks the skill rule 'never animate blur continuously / on large surfaces'. It is a real risk to 60fps on a laptop iGPU.
findings.evidence: graph-explorer.tsx:175 `rounded-xl bg-card ring-1 ring-border backdrop-blur-md` and :260 the same on the aside. graph-canvas.tsx:453 `pill = '... bg-card/90 ... backdrop-blur-sm'` and :546 cluster label `backdrop-blur-[2px]`. index.css:12 `--card: oklch(0.985 0.005 85 / 0.76)`. Not profiled.
findings.fix: Delete `backdrop-blur-*` from the canvas container, the aside, the pill constant and the cluster labels. Give the canvas container an opaque surface (`bg-popover`, an existing opaque token, index.css:14) so the fog's PAPER colour matches what is actually behind it.

findings.area: Demo legibility: the hero path shows raw ids
findings.issue: ALS is the first suggestion, but all 10 of its embedding neighbours have no label and render as 'MESH:D000544' and so on. Six of its 44 stored graph neighbours are unlabelled too, as are 12 of Riluzole's 44 and 9 of SOD1's 44. Judges will see a column of MeSH codes exactly where Alzheimer's and Parkinson's should be. The data report confirms the cause: only 128 of 5,103 diseases are labelled, and nothing in the raw data maps MeSH ids to names.
findings.evidence: I decoded shard 25 in node: ALS knn = Disease::MESH:D000544, D012559, D010300, D011085, D000437, D009103, D029424, D053713, D001172, D014029, all unlabelled. buildSearch :154 falls back to `id.slice(id.indexOf('::') + 2)`.
findings.fix: Data-side, smallest fix: add a hand-curated MeSH→name map to names-extra.json for the highest-degree Disease::MESH ids. At minimum cover the neighbours of ALS, Riluzole, Edaravone, SOD1 and TARDBP, about 100 entries. That keeps the UI unchanged. Mark them as curated in drkg_graph.py.

findings.area: Legibility at arm's length (AGENTS working style)
findings.issue: The main orientation text is set at 11–12 px: the in-scene island labels, the entity pills, the legend rows and counts, the layout footnote, inspector row details and dt labels, and search-result ids. At an expo table that won't read at arm's length. The island labels are the only thing explaining what the dust is.
findings.evidence: graph-canvas.tsx:546 `text-[0.6875rem]` (island labels), :453 pill `text-xs`. graph-explorer.tsx:236 legend rows `text-xs`, :252 footnote `text-[0.6875rem]`. graph-inspector.tsx:39, :162, :279, :294 `text-[0.6875rem]`. graph-search.tsx:156.
findings.fix: Correct the values: island labels and pills to `text-sm` (14px), legend rows to `text-sm`, and keep 11px only for secondary metadata like ids. Island labels are already collision-culled, so larger text costs nothing structurally.

findings.area: Layout: footnote overlaps legend on narrower laptops
findings.issue: The legend is anchored at `bottom-12` (48px). The footnote is at `bottom-3` with full width and about 190 characters of 11px text. Canvas width is the viewport minus the 18rem sidebar, the 23rem aside and the gaps, about 560px at 1280 wide, so the footnote wraps to 2–3 lines (about 38–53px tall) and reaches about 50–65px from the bottom. That paints over the legend's last row (Tax). Both are z-10, and the footnote comes later in the DOM.
findings.evidence: graph-explorer.tsx:217 `absolute bottom-12 left-3 z-10 w-52` and :252 `absolute bottom-3 left-3 z-10 max-w-[calc(100%-1.5rem)] ... text-[0.6875rem] leading-snug`. Computed, not verified in the browser.
findings.fix: Put both in one bottom-left flex column (`absolute bottom-3 left-3 flex flex-col gap-2`) so they stack instead of using fixed offsets. Or shorten the footnote to one line and move the layout caveat into the inspector's empty state.

findings.area: Hover: re-render per pointermove, pick order, stale tooltip
findings.issue: There are four problems. (a) onHover sets a fresh object on every pointermove, even when the row hasn't changed, so GraphCanvas re-renders its whole overlay (24 island divs, labels, tooltip) at pointer rate. (b) pick() returns the first visible hit in R3F order, which is by camera distance, so it picks the front-most point inside the 0.09 cylinder rather than the one under the cursor. In dense islands that is often the wrong point. (c) While dragging, onPointerMove returns early without clearing hover, and nothing updates the tooltip during the camera fly or autoRotate, so it stays frozen over a point that has moved. (d) The tooltip is never clamped, so near the right or bottom edge it is cut off by the container's overflow-hidden.
findings.evidence: :432-436 `onHover(row === null ? null : { row, x: e.nativeEvent.offsetX, y: ... })`. :420-424 loops `e.intersections` in order. :433 `if (ui.current.dragging) return`. :565 `translate3d(${hover.x + 14}px, ...)` with no clamp.
findings.fix: (a) Keep the tooltip position in a ref and write `style.transform` directly. Call setHover only when the row changes. (b) Among visible hits, take the minimum `hit.distanceToRay`, with lit rows first. (c) Call onHover(null) in the controls' 'start' listener and when `s.flying` begins. (d) Flip to the left/top when x + width > size.width.

findings.area: Keyboard: Alt+Arrow hijacked inside the search field
findings.issue: The window keydown handler calls preventDefault and steps history on Alt+Left/Right even while the search input is focused. On macOS, Option+Arrow is word-jump in text fields, so moving the cursor through a query unexpectedly navigates the selection. The handler already computes `typing` but only uses it for Escape.
findings.evidence: graph-explorer.tsx:86-89 `const typing = ...; if (e.altKey && (e.key === 'ArrowLeft' || e.key === 'ArrowRight')) { e.preventDefault(); step(...) }`
findings.fix: Change the condition to `if (e.altKey && !typing && (...))`.

findings.area: Per-frame DOM work (fixing-motion-performance: measurement)
findings.issue: Every frame, useFrame writes `style.opacity` and a freshly built `style.transform` string for every island label and pill, even when the camera is still. The render loop never stops: it runs at 60fps forever and autoRotates after 20 s. The first offsetWidth/offsetHeight read for each new label happens inside the same frame, right after transform writes to earlier labels, so it forces a synchronous style/layout pass for each new label on every selection change (up to about 13).
findings.evidence: :392-393 `if (!d) dims.set(el, (d = [el.offsetWidth, el.offsetHeight]))` inside `put`, which is interleaved with :405-406 style writes.
findings.fix: Measure the new label elements in a useLayoutEffect on `labels` (one batched read) instead of inside useFrame. In useFrame, skip label placement when `camera.matrixWorld` hasn't changed since the last frame, by comparing against a cached Matrix4.

findings.area: Camera double flight on first visit to a shard
findings.issue: On selection, `graph` is null until the shard promise resolves, so the canvas effect first flies to the lone selection (want clamps to 7). When neighbours arrive it recomputes goal and distance, and the camera changes course mid-flight. Toggling 'Draw' for embedding neighbours also re-frames the camera, because knn is in the effect's dependencies.
findings.evidence: graph-explorer.tsx:82 `const graph = entity && entity.row === selected ? entity.graph : null` and :97-103. graph-canvas.tsx:281-340 effect deps include `neighbours, knn`.
findings.fix: Only set `ui.current.flying = true` / recompute the goal when `selected` changes or when neighbours go from null to loaded for the same selection. Skip it for knn toggles. A `prevSelected` ref is enough.

findings.area: Shortest working diff: dead code and unused exports
findings.issue: VIEWS.graph (title, description and 'coming soon' placeholder) is unreachable now that `view === 'graph'` renders GraphExplorer before the placeholder branch. graph-canvas.tsx re-exports TypeGlyph from drkg-legend purely as an indirection. `GRAPH_DIR` and `decodeShard` are exported but only used inside graph-data.ts. The expression `ids && ids.length === n ? ids : null` appears three times in graph-explorer.tsx.
findings.evidence: Home.tsx:22-26 VIEWS.graph and :165-166 the graph branch. graph-canvas.tsx:46 `export { TypeGlyph }`. A grep shows GRAPH_DIR and decodeShard referenced only in graph-data.ts. graph-explorer.tsx:52, :207, :266.
findings.fix: Delete VIEWS.graph. Import TypeGlyph from '@/components/discovery/drkg-legend' directly. Drop the `export` keyword on GRAPH_DIR and decodeShard. Compute `const idsOk = ids && ids.length === n ? ids : null` once.
